source.title: Rethinking Batch Normalization in Transformers
source.authors: Sheng Shen; Zhe-Wei Yao; A. Gholami; Michael W. Mahoney; K. Keutzer

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies normalization in NLP transformers and reports task performance, but does not measure the classification training error, convergence speed, learning-rate tolerance, or other behavior specified by V1–V6.
record.gate_note: The paper reports BLEU and perplexity comparisons among normalization methods. Those are task-performance results, not the training-error, training-speed, or learning-rate outcomes named in the versions. The cited prior studies on batch normalization are not this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study compares normalization methods using held-out BLEU and perplexity, batch-statistic fluctuations, gradient components, and conditional smoothness arguments. It does not measure training speed or learning-rate tolerance against an otherwise identical unnormalized network, or any other outcome specified by V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors attribute vanilla BN's poor NLP transformer performance partly to fluctuating batch statistics and report that PN outperforms LN on the tested translation and language-modeling benchmarks. They also establish conditional theoretical properties for PN-V and PN.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares alternative normalization schemes in NLP transformers and reports task performance; it does not reproduce the classification-training recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and task change the reported metric and values; in the IWSLT14 batch-size ablation, normalization performance varies with mini-batch size, as described in text and Figure 5.

fits_no_version.finding: BN yields lower translation BLEU than LN; PN yields higher BLEU. PN-V ties LN on IWSLT14 in Table 1 and underperforms it on WMT14.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization choice changes held-out translation performance in the tested transformers with encoder normalization replaced and decoder LN retained.

fits_no_version.finding: BN yields higher test perplexity than LN on PTB and WikiText-103; PN yields lower test perplexity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization choice changes held-out perplexity in the tested tensorized language models.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 2–4 show larger batch-statistic discrepancies and persistent gradient-component outliers in the NLP transformer than in ResNet20, with reduced fluctuations under PN-V.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch-statistic and gradient-component variability depend on the model, task, and normalization scheme.

fits_no_version.finding: Lemma 2 establishes a conditional gradient-norm reduction for PN-V; Theorem 4 bounds PN's approximate gradients under explicit assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Power normalization has conditional smoothness and bounded-gradient properties; these results alone do not establish faster training or greater learning-rate tolerance.

record.problems: The reported results are task metrics rather than training classification error or convergence speed. Some layer-normalized language-model values are marked as the authors' own implementation with an asterisk; uncertainty estimates are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the reported normalization comparison tables. Figure 5 batch-size values are figure-only and are described qualitatively in the text, but are not extracted as numerical rows.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and recipe-dependent failures.
Spurious minima and extra student width in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training error with and without identity shortcuts, and special initialization or normalization-free residual training.
Initialization-dependent training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Loss, curvature, recovery, and divergence relative to the learning-rate stability threshold.
BN versus no normalization on training speed and learning-rate tolerance; Fixup's normalization-free training speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is warranted for V1–V6. The record's blanket statement that no normalization-table rows were omitted overlooks additional comparators in Table 4 and validation results in Table 3, but these do not bear on any version. Appendix A qualifies the main text's replacement description: translation changes encoder normalization only, and PN-specific moving-average coefficients are tuned on validation data.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification training error, random or corrupted labels, model size, training duration, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious minima, and student width.
Depth-related training error in plain and residual networks, shortcuts, and the Fixup or special-initialization cases.
Initialization effects on training speed and trainable depth.
Training loss and curvature dynamics at or above the stability limit.
Training speed, accuracy over training time, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's normalization-free residual training.
